column1: # Findings of the ZAP baseline scan (CI job "dast", tests/zap/scan.sh) that are known and accepted. Tab separated:
# rule id, level (IGNORE = false positive or only caused by the test server, WARN = real but accepted), name of the alert
# exactly as in the report, reason. A finding of risk medium or higher that has no line here fails the job
# (tests/zap/check.py), as does a line without a reason. Fix a finding rather than list it; remove a line when the
# finding is gone for good (the job prints a note for lines without a finding in the run).

column4: The admin interface (Filament 5, Livewire 4, Alpine) writes inline scripts and event attributes into every page, and the portal and public forms use inline event handlers (onsubmit, oninput) and two inline scripts (proof of work, approvals). A policy without 'unsafe-inline' would need nonces, which do not cover event attributes. Scripts from other servers, plugins, a changed base address and forms sent elsewhere are forbidden (SecurityHeaders, SecurityHeadersTest).

Only sent for /admin: Alpine, which Livewire and Filament bring along, evaluates the expressions that Filament writes into x-data, x-on and x-show with new Function; the build of Alpine without evaluation does not support such expressions. All other pages get a policy without 'unsafe-eval' (SecurityHeadersTest).

Filament and Livewire set style attributes and inline style elements (colours of the panel, x-show, progress bar), and own views use style attributes (overviews of people and households, API reference). Styles from other servers are forbidden.

column3: Content Security Policy (CSP) Header Not Set
column4: Only on /api, /brand, /build and /build/assets: these are folders in public/, so the error page comes from the web server (here the built-in server of PHP), not from Kasmin, and holds no content of the application. Every answer of Kasmin itself has the policy (SecurityHeadersTest, also for errors and the API).

Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * is meant for /api/*: the public endpoints (events, forms) are read by the websites of the organisations, and all others need an API token in the Authorization header, never the session cookie (no Access-Control-Allow-Credentials), so another website cannot use the login of a visitor.
Only the XSRF-TOKEN cookie: scripts must read it to send it back as a request header (double submit; Livewire and Filament do so). The session cookie is HttpOnly.

Only on files of public/ (images, scripts, styles), which the built-in server of PHP answers in this scan. On a real web server public/.htaccess adds the header to them; every answer of Kasmin has it (SecurityHeadersTest).

column3: Server Leaks Information via "X-Powered-By" HTTP Response Header Field(s)
column4: Only on files and folders of public/ answered by the built-in server of PHP in this scan; a real web server answers them without PHP. Kasmin removes the header from its own answers.

column3: Big Redirect Detected (Potential Sensitive Information Leak)
column4: False positive: the body is the standard page of the framework for redirects ("Redirecting to" with the same address as the Location header), nothing else.
Only on scripts and folders of public/ answered by the web server; the header matters for documents, and every page of Kasmin has it (SecurityHeadersTest).

False positive: the numbers are the expiry time in the proof-of-work task of public forms (meant to be read by the browser) and identifiers of Livewire components in the admin interface (wire:key), no times.
The profile page of the portal shows logged-in people the address of their own sessions; in this scan that is the address of the scanner in the docker network.

Not set on purpose: images of mails (/mail-images) are loaded by webmail of other websites, and pictures and forms of public events are shown on the websites of the organisations; "same-origin" would break both. Reading answers from another website is prevented by the missing CORS permission for everything outside /api.
Only needed for cross-origin isolation (SharedArrayBuffer), which Kasmin does not use; "require-corp" would only add a way to break pages. Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy is set.
